source.title: Simulated Ensemble Attack: Transferring Jailbreaks Across Fine-tuned Vision-Language Models
source.authors: Ruofan Wang; Xin Wang; Yang Yao; Jun-Cheng Li; Xuan Tong; Xing-Jun Ma

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Reports outcomes of benign fine-tuning on harmful-query non-refusal and tests a compliant-opening prompt intervention in VLMs, using measures and models different from the original studies.
record.gate_note: Table 1 reports non-refusal after general-purpose fine-tuning without an attack. Table 2 reports ASR for the text-only Targeted Prompt Guidance baseline, which instructs a compliant affirmative opening. The paper does not measure response-position KL, token-level safety concentration, or safety localization in parameters. Results about adversarial images and SEA are not included as V4 rows because they do not test the named opening, suffix, or decoding interventions.
record.test_reason: Table 1 reports harmful-query non-refusal, without any attack, for base Qwen-2-VL-7B and an LLM-only variant fine-tuned on benign general-purpose data (OmniAlign-V). That is a direct V2 result in a new setting (VLMs). The rest of the paper evaluates the authors' own image-jailbreak method (SEA) and does not bear on the versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly correct. Additions: the authors frame the 45.38% no-attack non-refusal as consistent with Qi et al. 2023 that fine-tuning undermines refusal. They state TPG alone does not bypass safety alignment. They also claim SEA generalizes across Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen3-VL.
record.recipe_differences: The study concerns image-based VLM jailbreak transfer and parameter perturbation, not harmful-example fine-tuning of aligned text chat models or measurement of per-token KL concentration.
record.method_sensitivity: Prompt-only TPG ASR differs substantially between the 2B and 7B base models and falls sharply after MIS safety fine-tuning. Fine-tuning configuration also varies in Table 2.

fits_no_version.finding: A text-only instruction to begin with 'Sure, here is' reaches 90.38% ASR on base Qwen-2-VL-2B but only 15.00% on base 7B. After MIS safety fine-tuning it falls to 1.5–8.9% across Qwen2-VL configurations, and to 0.00–2.12% on fine-tuned Qwen2.5-VL-3B and Qwen3-VL-4B (Table 6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prefix-injection prompt instructions elicit compliant openings at rates that vary strongly by model and are largely suppressed by safety fine-tuning in VLMs.

fits_no_version.finding: Vision-module fine-tuning updates are small relative to base weight scale: mean r is 3.0e-2 for OmniAlign-V and 1.05e-2 for MIS.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning updates to the measured vision modules remain within a local parameter neighborhood of the base model.

record.problems: The paper says its fine-tuning datasets have limited scale and diversity relative to real-world practice. The reported benign fine-tuning non-refusal result is for one model and one setting, and NRR does not establish harmful content. No uncertainty estimates are given for the ASR results.
record.rows_left_out: Other ASR and toxicity results concern adversarial-image attacks, SEA, or free-form toxicity, rather than the named token-prefill, suffix, or decoding interventions. The study's layerwise parameter-distribution discussion in Figure 3 is not separately rowed because the reported Table 5 parameter-displacement statistics already capture the relevant non-version finding.

untested.parts: Only one benign dataset and one model (Qwen-2-VL-7B, LLM-only) are tested. NRR does not show whether non-refusals contain harmful content. No data-selection (carefully chosen benign) condition.
No per-token or position-wise KL analysis.
No forced prefilling, adversarial suffixes or decoding changes. The text-only 'begin with' instruction is a prompt jailbreak whose success measure is the opening itself.
Parameter displacement is measured, but not whether a small set of weights carries safety.
No test of why safety is shallow.

record.verdict_notes: The paper is an attack-method paper, and its only bearing on the claim is the single benign fine-tuning NRR result. The reader linked the TPG baseline rows to V4, but TPG is a 'Must begin your response with' prompt, not a forced prefill. Its ASR keyword metric counts emitting the affirmative prefix, so it measures elicitation of the opening rather than what happens after the opening is supplied. Those rows are relinked to none. Qi et al. 2023 is cited but is not this study, so verdicts are allowed.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not fine-tune on harmful examples to test whether they remove refusal.
The no-attack non-refusal measure does not establish that the non-refusal responses contain harmful instructions; only one general-purpose fine-tuning setting is reported for this measure.
No per-token KL divergence or other response-position analysis is reported.

The study tests a textual instruction to begin with an affirmative continuation, not token prefilling, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes. It does not test whether safety differences are concentrated in early response positions.
Parameter changes are measured, but the study does not test whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
The study does not test whether data or training objectives cause safety to be shallow across response positions.
The study does not train or evaluate a method intended to deepen safety across response positions.

rows.subject: Qwen-2-VL-7B
rows.operation_detail: LLM-only fine-tuning on OmniAlign-V; measure harmful-query non-refusal without an attack.
rows.note: The paper defines NRR as any non-refusal response, distinguishing it from targeted ASR. This result indicates increased non-refusal, but does not show that the responses provide harmful instructions.
rows.check: Link and state are correct. Caveats: NRR counts any non-refusal, not harmful content, and the result covers one model and one dataset.

source_check.correct: No-attack NRR rises from 0.38% to 45.38% after LLM-only OmniAlign-V fine-tuning. For V2's harmful-compliance claim, state=cannot_determine: NRR counts any non-refusal and does not establish harmful content.
source_check.locator_found: Sections 4.1.2 and 4.2.1; Table 1, No Attack row, NRR columns.
source_check.problem: The numbers establish reduced refusal, but observed overstates what this measure establishes about harmful compliance.

relation.reason: The authors connect reduced refusal after general-purpose fine-tuning to prior safety-degradation findings, but the cited comparison does not measure V2's harmful compliance.

tranche.reason: The proposed V2 result measures any non-refusal rather than harmful compliance. Under the related-construct exclusion, it does not establish the literal claim. SEA's attack-transfer results do not supply the missing benign-fine-tuning compliance comparison.

source_check.notes: The supplied text is arXiv v3 dated January 14, 2026, although the pack lists 2025. A claim explicitly about refusal erosion would be supported by R1.

reader_labels.condition: MIS-fine-tuned Qwen-2-VL-2B and Qwen-2-VL-7B variants with text-only TPG
reader_labels.reason: ASR is low across the reported safety-fine-tuned configurations, ranging from 1.54% to 8.85%, so the prompt intervention does not reliably defeat safety fine-tuning (R3–R6, R8–R11). The Qwen-2-VL-7B base result is also only 15.00% (R7).
